item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Aug 7 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (

item.description: Outfitting IU Athletics: Hoosier Champions This exhibit showcases objects from IU's championship teams and athletes, connecting them to historic achievements in the Big Ten and the national stage. Dates: November 14, 2025 - October 2026 By Their Own Hands: The Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame! Founded in 1974 by the Culture and Ethnic Affairs Guild of the Oakland Museum of California, the Black Filmmakers Hall of Fame began as a film lecture series and awards ceremony celebrating achievements of Black film industry figures. When that organization closed, they donated their materials to IU. In collaboration with the IU Black Film Center and Archive, this exhibit features objects from that collection, including founding documents, costumes

item.title: Terran Robotics 3D Adobe Printing Open House — Tue Aug 11, 3:00 PM
item.description:
Terraforming Indiana: Terran Robotics has started their 2nd 3D-printed, permitted adobe home in Bloomington, and they're inviting the community out to celebrate and see their earthen construction robotics in action.
Terran Robotics is a Bloomington-based startup building AI-guided robots that 3D-print homes from local adobe (clay, aggregate, and straw), aiming to make housing more affordable and sustainable.
Address available upon RSVP: https://partiful.com/e/lg2m6uzcsRu1h7DtOQ1i
Hosted by Danny and Ryan Zaricki.

item.title: Mindfulness at the Museum — Thu Aug 13, 2:00 PM — SIDNEY AND LOIS ESKENAZI MUSEUM OF ART
item.description:
Join us at the museum and mentally recenter by making art or journaling, and make some time to check in with yourself! Join us for a therapist-selected art activity meant to help you feel more balanced and in control. No prior skills needed, just bring your heart and mind. This group meets Thursday from 2–3 p.m., excluding holidays and museum closures. Meetings are held in the Atrium of the Sidney and Lois Eskenazi Museum of Art. Food and beverages are permitted in the atrium, so participants are welcome to bring lunch.

item.title: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, the Moment — Fri Aug 21 — LILLY LIBRARY
item.description: The Declaration of Independence: The Motives, The Momentexamines a crucial time in American history through the collections of the Lilly Library. The first printing of the Declaration of Independence, one of only twenty-six copies known today, is the centerpiece of the exhibition. Printed immediately for distribution, it is the source of all revolutionary era reprintings. The famous hand-written version was an official formality created later, signed in August, and stored away.Books, pamphlets, newspapers, prints, and letters allow viewers to explore key questions about this moment in time. How did a people proud to be in the British empire come to believe independence was possible or even desirable? What ideas and historical events did they draw on to justify resistance to Great Britain? What kinds of communication networks would be crucial for circulating the Declaration and countless other revolutionary documents throughout the colonies?This exhibition is part of America 250 at IU (
